description: Enterprise techniques used by APT38, ATT&CK group G0082 (v4.0)
name: APT38 (G0082)

techniques.comment: [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used the legitimate application `ieinstal.exe` to bypass UAC.(Citation: 1 - appv)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has executed persistence actions using `sudo` commands within zsh shells.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used Finder, a macOS native app with FDA permissions, to rename the folder `com.apple.TCC`, then used another process to move the `TCC.db` file to a new location, where SQLite3 was used to edit `TCC.db`. The edited `TCC.db` file allowed code signing authorization, permission access, etc. without requiring a user prompt.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has created fake domains to imitate legitimate venture capital or bank domains.(Citation: 1 - appv) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has acquired domains to host fake skill assessments leading to malware download.(Citation: Microsoft CYBERWARCON NOV 2024) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has registered domains that masquerade as financial institutions and resemble legitimate services.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also obtained C2 domains to host second-stage malicious payloads.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used virtual private server (VPS) providers to host C2 infrastructure including Hostwinds.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used OneDrive and GoogleDrive to host malicious files.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) used a backdoor, QUICKRIDE, to communicate to the C2 server over HTTP and HTTPS.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also configured malicious payloads to communicate with C2 using HTTP POST requests that blend in with common traffic.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has archived collected data within ZIP files prior to exfiltration.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also added registry run keys within `HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\MicrosoftUpdate` to enable persistence on Windows devices after reboot. (Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has executed a multiplatform implant that dropped a Registry Run key to `:\ProgramData\NodePackages\` for persistence on Windows machines.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has obtained boot- persistence on compromised systems independent of user logon by adding the registry key `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\services\scdev\Parameters`.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has collected browser bookmark information to learn more about compromised hosts, obtain personal information about users, and acquire details about internal network resources.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also used malware capable of enumerating 166 unique cryptocurrency wallets, browser extensions, and browser history.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used brute force techniques to attempt account access when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are unavailable.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) used a Trojan called KEYLIME to collect data from the clipboard.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used PowerShell to execute commands and other operational tasks.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also used PowerShell to establish persistence and establish C2 communication on compromised hosts.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has sent Mac users.scpt files to trigger malicious downloads.(Citation: Microsoft CYBERWARCON NOV 2024) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has targeted macOS uses with  native script stagers leading to malicious paylaods.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also used an AppleScript-based credential harvesting component.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used a command-line tunneler, NACHOCHEESE, to give them shell access to a victim’s machine.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018) Additionally, [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used batch scripts.(Citation: 1 - appv)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also executed scripts to launch `cmd.exe` to POST stolen data to actor-controlled domains.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has run malicious payloads using Linux and Unix shells. [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also executed Unix commands sequentially using `&&` and in the background with `&`.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026) (Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used VBScript to execute commands and other operational tasks.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)(Citation: 1 - appv) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has sent Windows victims Visual Basic script stagers leading to malicious downloads.(Citation: Microsoft CYBERWARCON NOV 2024)(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also used VBScript to execute scripts for data exfiltration.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used Python versions of its remote access tools on Linux targets.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has utilized malicious JavaScript payloads to compromise victims.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used virtual private server (VPS) providers to host C2 infrastructure including Hostwinds.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has executed a multiplatform implant that placed launch agents in ~/Library/NodePackages/  to establish persistence on macOS.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has installed a new Windows service to establish persistence.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has gained persistence on compromised systems independent of user logon by creating a background service using `sc create scdev binPath= "c:\windows\system32\svchost.exe -k scdev".(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has established persistence through storing the malicious plist files in `/Library/LaunchDaemons`.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has stolen credentials from the compromised device to include those used to access cryptocurrency wallets.(Citation: Microsoft CYBERWARCON NOV 2024)(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has stolen data stored in macOS keychain.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has gathered Web browser data to include saved credentials, cookies, bookmarks, autofill data, and extension-specific storage. [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also sought cryptocurrency wallet extensions.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used a custom secure delete function to make deleted files unrecoverable.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has utilized Base64 encoded HTTP POST communications to C2.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used Hermes ransomware to encrypt files with AES256.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has gathered Telegram Desktop messaging data from the applications data directories stored on the victim device to include cryptographic key material, and session mapping files that can recreate a compromised user’s Telegram session on another system.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has copied Apple Notes database from its application container and staged for upload.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has collected data from a compromised host.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used DYEPACK to create, delete, and alter records in databases used for SWIFT transactions.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used DYEPACK to manipulate SWIFT messages en route to a printer.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used DYEPACK.FOX to manipulate PDF data as it is accessed to remove traces of fraudulent SWIFT transactions from the data displayed to the end user.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has staged files in a central location prior to exfiltration.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has delayed C2 beaconing to longer intervals on network failures.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used the RC4 algorithm to decrypt configuration data. (Citation: 1 - appv) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has decocoded Base64 encoded PowerShell scripts prior to execution.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) have created firewall exemptions on specific ports, including ports 443, 6443, 8443, and 9443.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) have created firewall exemptions on specific ports, including ports 443, 6443, 8443, and 9443. (Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has unhooked DLLs to disable endpoint detection and response (EDR) or anti-virus (AV) tools.(Citation: 1 - appv)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has displayed a fake “system update complete” dialog to the user following successful deployment of malicious payloads.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) clears Window Event logs and Sysmon logs from the system.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used a custom MBR wiper named BOOTWRECK to render systems inoperable.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has conducted watering holes schemes to gain initial access to victims.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used professional platforms such as LinkedIn to contact potential victims.(Citation: Microsoft CYBERWARCON NOV 2024)(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has set up anonymous emails to use in publishing poisoned software packages such as sergey2016@tutamail[.]com.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has poisoned Axios and Mastra npm packages with malicious post-install hooks.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has leveraged file discovery actions to determine if a predetermined file is present prior to execution to prevent redundant execution on a compromised device.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has created a mutex to avoid duplicate execution.(Citation: 1 - appv)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used malware to exfiltrate stolen data with a custom ICAP-style protocol over HTTPS.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has exfiltrated victim device and user details contained in a POST request to register the compromised system with C2 infrastructure.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has exfiltrated stolen credentials to actor-controlled infrastructure leveraging Telegram Bot API.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has enumerated files and directories, or searched in specific locations within a compromised host.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has changed file and directory permissions using `chmod 777`.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has conducted cryptocurrency theft.(Citation: Microsoft CYBERWARCON NOV 2024)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has created decoy content that resembles legitimate guidance for support to victims that contain hidden malicious actions.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has created fictitious profiles on social media utilizing fake photos and personas to entice users to engage in the schemes.(Citation: Microsoft CYBERWARCON NOV 2024)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has configured malicious scripts to execute in hidden windows.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used remote access tools that run AppleScript using ` nohup osascript` to ignore hangup signals.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has added Microsoft Defender exclusions to include `C:\Windows\System32` to suppress detection of dropped tooling.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has executed scripts to delete the PowerShell command history file.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used a utility called CLOSESHAVE that can securely delete a file from the system. [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also removed malware, tools, scripts, or other non-native files used during the intrusion to reduce their footprint or as part of the post-intrusion cleanup process.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has modified data timestamps to mimic files that are in the same folder on a compromised host.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) used a backdoor, NESTEGG, that has the capability to download and upload files to and from a victim’s machine.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018) Additionally, [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has downloaded other payloads onto a victim’s machine.(Citation: 1 - appv) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also injected npm packages with malicious dependencies that download second-stage payloads to victim machines.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) used a Trojan called KEYLIME to capture keystrokes from the victim’s machine.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has leveraged a fictitious native macOS password dialog prompt to entice victims to enter credentials.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has renamed system utilities, such as `rundll32.exe` and `mshta.exe`, to avoid detection.(Citation: 1 - appv)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has named malicious payloads as benign-looking executables to blend in the environment including Run keys, npm packages, and JavaScript utilities often using names mirroring Apple, Windows, or other native system files.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has put several spaces before a file extension to avoid detection and suspicion.(Citation: 1 - appv)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has configured malware to rename malicious payloads with naming conventions that reduce a chance of detection to include renaming “package.md” to “package.json”.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) uses a tool called CLEANTOAD that has the capability to modify Registry keys.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used the Windows API to execute code within a victim's system.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has enumerated network shares on a compromised host.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has leveraged unique non-standard ports for communications with actor-controlled C2 infrastructure to include Port 8000.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used several code packing methods such as Themida, Enigma, VMProtect, and Obsidium, to pack their implants.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has utilized Base64 encoded PowerShell scripts.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has compressed its malicious payloads in ZIP files for delivery to victims.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has added thousands of blank lines to scripts to push malicious logic past the scrollable view of the script editor.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has obtained and used open-source tools such as [Mimikatz](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0002).(Citation: ESET Lazarus KillDisk April 2018)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has conducted spearphishing campaigns using malicious email attachments.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has sent fake Zoom support emails with malicious attachments.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has sent phishing emails with invite links to fictitious meetings.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used social media sites such as LinkedIn  to send malicious links to potential vicitims.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has poisoned npm packages with fake runtime dependencies to trigger execution of malicious payloads on developer endpoints or continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) systems during npm installation or update.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has prepended a space to all of their terminal commands to operate without leaving traces in the HISTCONTROL environment.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has prevented logging and muted error logs through the use of `/dev/null 2>&1 &`. (Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also executed scripts to delete the PowerShell command history file and to prevent future history recording using `-Force Set-PSReadLineOption -HistorySaveStyle SaveNothing`.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) leveraged Sysmon to understand the processes, services in the organization.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used Python versions of its remote access tools on Linux targets.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also configured malicious payloads to gather running processes using `ps aux`.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has injected malicious payloads into the `explorer.exe` process.(Citation: 1 - appv) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also injected malicious binaries directly into memory on compromised hosts.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has run node.js malware to query the Registry to discover installed software.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has configured malicious payloads to reflectively load using the macOS `NSCreateObjectFileImageFromMemory` API.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also reflectively loaded .NET DLLs to bypass disk-based detection.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used cron to create pre-scheduled and periodic background jobs on a Linux system.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used Task Scheduler to run programs at system startup or on a scheduled basis for persistence.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020) Additionally, [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used living-off-the-land scripts to execute a malicious script via a scheduled task.(Citation: 1 - appv)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used a multiplatform implant that can write to `~/.config/systemd/nvmconf/` to gain persistence on Linux hosts.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used web shells for persistence or to ensure redundant access.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has impersonated recruiters and venture capitalists to lure victims into connecting to malicious skills assessments or online business meetings.(Citation: Microsoft CYBERWARCON NOV 2024)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has enumerated installed applications to build an inventory of the system’s software environment.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has identified security software, configurations, defensive tools, and sensors installed on a compromised system.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)(Citation: 1 - appv) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also executed malware implants to enumerate all installed applications on Windows hosts including installed security products.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has uploaded malware to cloud storage services for download by targeted victims.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used ISO and VHD files to deploy malware and to bypass Mark-of-the-Web (MOTW) security measures.(Citation: 1 - appv)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has injected malicious dependencies into software packages such as Axios and Mastra npm packages.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used CHM files to move concealed payloads.(Citation: Kaspersky Lazarus Under The Hood APR 2017)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used a renamed version of `mshta.exe` to execute malicious HTML files.(Citation: 1 - appv)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used `msiexec.exe` to execute malicious files.(Citation: 1 - appv)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used rundll32.exe to execute binaries, scripts, and Control Panel Item files and to execute code via proxy to avoid triggering security tools.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020)(Citation: 1 - appv)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has attempted to get detailed information about a compromised host, including the operating system, version, patches, hotfixes, and service packs.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has executed malware to collect current user, host name, system time, and operating system install date from targeted systems.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) installed a port monitoring tool, MAPMAKER, to print the active TCP connections on the local system.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has identified primary users, currently logged in users, sets of users that commonly use a system, or inactive users.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has run malware to enumerate the current user on compromised hosts.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has created new services or modified existing ones to run executables, commands, or scripts.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has also installed a persistent service on targeted hosts to load malicious DLLs at boot.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used a custom MBR wiper named BOOTWRECK, which will initiate a system reboot after wiping the victim's MBR.(Citation: FireEye APT38 Oct 2018)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has run malware to discover the system time on compromised hosts.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has gathered data and credentials stored in Shell History.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has gathered cryptographic key data related to cryptocurrency wallets, SSH keys, and messaging applications to include Telegram.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used links to execute a malicious Visual Basic script.(Citation: 1 - appv) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has directed users to navigate to a website under adversary control through the sharing of links in messages.(Citation: Microsoft CYBERWARCON NOV 2024)(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082)  has attempted to lure victims into enabling malicious macros within email attachments.(Citation: CISA AA20-239A BeagleBoyz August 2020) Additionally, [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used malicious Word documents and shortcut files.(Citation: 1 - appv) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has lured victims into opening malicious .scpt or .vbs files to fix fake connection issues with online meetings.(Citation: Microsoft CYBERWARCON NOV 2024)(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026) [APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used social media invites to lure victims into opening malicious files hosted on cloud infrastructure.(Citation: Microsoft Axios Compromise APR 2026)

[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has validated stolen credentials against the local macOS authentication database using directory services prior to exfiltration.(Citation: Microsoft Sapphire Sleet APR 2026)
[APT38](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0082) has used victim maintainer accounts for the npm Registry to publish malicious packages.(Citation: MIcrosoft Mastra npm Compromise JUN 2026)
